inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,338 logical lines of the normalized source. The notes form a continuous semantic chain from zeta sums, through Taylor polynomialization, bilinear variable duplication, and Vinogradov mean-value estimates, to zeta bounds, the Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free region, and the prime-number-theorem error term. Prose and displayed formulas are generally recoverable, but embedded extraction control separators split several mathematical relations across logical lines, so formula-sensitive downstream use should retain the exact spans.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the lecture block's route from exponential-sum estimates to a zero-free region and a prime-number-theorem consequence.

sections_inspected.label: 7. First thoughts on estimating zeta sums
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reduces zeta control to short oscillatory sums and inserts a polynomial phase by averaging small bilinear shifts and Taylor expanding.

sections_inspected.label: 8. Bilinear forms
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops completion, rational-spacing bounds, and repeated Hölder duplication as a way to turn sparse polynomial-curve sums into mean-value counts and one-dimensional geometric sums.

sections_inspected.label: 9. Vinogradov's Mean Value Theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces the mean value, compares diagonal and volume lower bounds, proves the congruence and translation tools, and executes a scale-reducing induction with nonsingular and singular residue branches.

sections_inspected.label: 10. Second thoughts on estimating zeta sums
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Combines the preceding reductions, chooses parameters, exploits rational approximation in a useful degree window, and obtains a nontrivial zeta-sum estimate.

sections_inspected.label: 11. Some spectacular (?) consequences
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers zeta-sum cancellation to a near-one-line zeta bound, a zero-free region, and the optimized prime-number-theorem error term, then explains the remaining gap to RH.

accepted_units.title: Zeta control becomes a short oscillatory-sum problem
accepted_units.why_material: It identifies the causal entry point of the method: a bound left of the one-line feeds Landau's theorem, while partial summation reduces the needed zeta estimate to sums of n^{-it} even at scales much shorter than t, where integral approximation fails.
accepted_units.context_note: Retain the stated dependency on the earlier Hardy–Littlewood approximation and Landau theorem; those results are referenced but not reproved in this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-to-moderate formula dependence; the prose recovers the reduction and the failure of the long-sum integral heuristic.

accepted_units.title: Small bilinear shifts polynomialize the logarithmic phase
accepted_units.why_material: Averaging n by shifts xy creates a small ratio xy/n, so a controlled Taylor truncation converts the unstructured logarithmic phase into a polynomial in xy. The required degree grows like log t/log N, explicitly exposing the method's later capacity bottleneck.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact exponents in the shift and truncation error are inessential according to the source; the degree-to-scale relation is essential.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence for constants and errors, but the shift–Taylor mechanism and degree obstruction are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Two independent shifts create reorderable bilinear structure
accepted_units.why_material: The source isolates a reusable design principle: introduce two independent variables even when one suffices for Taylor expansion, because later inequalities can alternately complete and move either variable family inside absolute values.
accepted_units.context_note: Its payoff is demonstrated in Lemma 8.3 and Remark 8.4, so this short span should be interpreted with that forward link.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-only and robust to notation changes.

accepted_units.title: Bilinear completion trades a sparse prime sum for an integer correlation sum
accepted_units.why_material: The toy proposition exhibits the basic move: complete one side of a bilinear sum, apply Cauchy–Schwarz, expand a square into differences, and bound the resulting geometric progressions by distance to the nearest integer.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposition's prime variables are illustrative; the reusable content is the completion–correlation–spacing pipeline.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependence; exact inequalities require the displayed sums, while the transformation is explained in prose.

accepted_units.title: Rational approximation distributes phases into controlled spacing bins
accepted_units.why_material: Coprimality permutes residue classes, and a small perturbation from a/q places only O(1) phases in each interval of width 1/q; isolating the near-zero bin and harmonically summing the rest yields the key min(U,1/||·||) bound.
accepted_units.context_note: This proof supplies the spacing estimate used both by the toy bilinear bound and the final product over polynomial degrees.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependence; interval locations and the exceptional near-zero bin are legible.

accepted_units.title: Repeated Hölder duplication regularizes sparse polynomial-curve vectors
accepted_units.why_material: The sparse vectors (x,x²,…,x^r) cannot simply be completed to a box. Two Hölder steps duplicate each variable family, turn sums of curve points into difference coordinates, dominate shifted counts by the central Vinogradov mean value, and finally factor the phase into estimable one-dimensional sums.
accepted_units.context_note: The long derivation is retained because switching summation order, bounding shifted counts, and duplicating the second variable are jointly the mechanism rather than routine algebra.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence for exponents and ranges; prose clearly states why duplication improves coverage and why two independent families matter.

accepted_units.title: Diagonal and volume counts predict the Vinogradov mean-value threshold
accepted_units.why_material: Two structurally different lower bounds—diagonal solutions and average occupancy of difference boxes—motivate a two-term conjecture. Their crossover explains why k at least about r(r+1)/2 is the regime needed for near-uniform behavior.
accepted_units.context_note: The cited modern result is contextual; the notes deliberately use an older bound whose dependence on growing k and r suits the zeta application.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependence; the two mechanisms and threshold comparison are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: A quantitative mean-value bound is organized as induction through congruences
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem gives the explicit loss parameter governing the application, and the proof preview identifies the core architecture: fix degree, induct in variable count, reduce modulo a scale-matched prime, and invoke Linnik's lemma.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is weaker than the conjectural optimum but is asserted to be sufficient for the later zeta estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence for the stated exponent and delta; the induction architecture is prose-stable.

accepted_units.title: Power sums plus distinct residues rigidify a tuple modulo a prime power
accepted_units.why_material: Congruences at different powers are first lifted to a common modulus. Newton identities convert power sums into elementary symmetric data, so the associated monic polynomials agree modulo p; distinct roots then force tuples to agree up to permutation modulo p^r.
accepted_units.context_note: The distinct-mod-p hypothesis is indispensable and later separates the nonsingular from the singular residue branch.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate-to-high formula dependence; the polynomial-root rigidity argument remains clear.

accepted_units.title: The power-sum system is translation invariant
accepted_units.why_material: Subtracting a common center preserves every balanced power-sum equation because each binomial coefficient term is itself a lower-degree balanced equation. This permits residue classes to be normalized before scale reduction.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof uses the entire hierarchy of equations through degree r, not only the top-degree relation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependence; the semantic invariance is explicit and notation-robust.

accepted_units.title: The nonsingular residue branch freezes a class and applies Linnik at the matched scale
accepted_units.why_material: Choosing p approximately Z^{1/r} matches Linnik's p^r range to the variable scale. Solutions with enough distinct residues are symmetrized, most residue classes are frozen using an integral/Hölder argument, translated to zero, and bounded by Linnik times a lower-variable mean value.
accepted_units.context_note: This span includes the proof of the residue-freezing claim because it is the bridge between a global count and the scale-reduced configuration.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence for constants and exponents; the prime-scale choice and freeze–translate–count mechanism are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: The singular residue branch gains by occupying too few classes
accepted_units.why_material: When either half lacks r distinct residues, the number of admissible residue patterns drops. Hölder bounds each pattern by a common-class moment, and translation followed by division by p turns that moment into a smaller-scale Vinogradov count.
accepted_units.context_note: This complementary branch shows that failure of nonsingularity is not discarded but becomes its own source of compression.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence for the final exponent comparison; the residue-pattern and divide-by-p mechanism is recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Iterating scale descent proves the quantitative mean-value theorem
accepted_units.why_material: The induction separates the trivial small-scale regime from the scale-reduction regime and tracks how the loss parameter changes when k is reduced by r and Z is replaced by a power of Z.
accepted_units.context_note: The source marks the details non-examinable, but the base/step split and exponent bookkeeping complete the theorem used later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence; exact exponents should be checked against the displayed relations.

accepted_units.title: Three reductions define the final zeta-sum pipeline
accepted_units.why_material: The source explicitly composes the argument: Taylor reduction produces U(n), Hölder duplication reduces U(n) to a mean value plus spacing sums, and the mean-value theorem supplies control when k is sufficiently large relative to r.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an author-provided synthesis rather than a new proof step and is useful for preserving the dependency graph.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-to-moderate formula dependence.

accepted_units.title: A rational-approximation degree window converts mean-value savings into zeta-sum cancellation
accepted_units.why_material: After setting k proportional to r², the mean-value theorem supplies a global negative exponent. For degrees in a selected window, the explicit Taylor coefficients admit rational approximants with denominators in a favorable range, giving extra spacing savings; choosing the proportionality constant controls delta and makes the negative term dominate losses.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact constant is existential and the source assumes the trivial small-N range away; preserve the conditions when reusing the estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependence. Embedded separators split several comparison symbols, but the prose and adjacent formulas recover the parameter logic; exact numerical reuse warrants source-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: The zeta-sum bound's strength is diagnosed by the N-versus-t scale
accepted_units.why_material: For N=t^theta the estimate gives a power saving, while below every fixed power it remains nontrivial only down to an exponential-in-log(t) threshold. The source contrasts this with the square-root cancellation heuristic.
accepted_units.context_note: This interprets rather than strengthens Theorem 10.1 and makes its operative range explicit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependence; qualitative scale distinctions are clear.

accepted_units.title: Block decomposition transfers short-sum cancellation to a near-one-line zeta bound
accepted_units.why_material: The Hardy–Littlewood approximation is split into exponentially sized blocks; Abel summation imports the zeta-sum estimate into each weighted block, and a second grouping makes the block series summable. A different splitting point handles sigma farther from one.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem depends on an earlier approximation outside this source. Both sigma regimes are retained because the split point changes with distance from one.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence for the final exponent and block endpoints; the decomposition and summability mechanism are explicit.

accepted_units.title: A controlled growth strip feeds Landau's theorem to widen the zero-free region
accepted_units.why_material: The zeta bound is rewritten in exponential form on a restricted strip, matched to Landau's phi and width functions, and converted into the Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free boundary.
accepted_units.context_note: The bounded-height completion is delegated to earlier known zero-free regions and symmetry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence for the logarithmic exponents; the theorem-to-zero-free transfer is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Contour truncation is balanced against the zero-free decay to optimize the PNT error
accepted_units.why_material: Shifting the prime-number-theorem contour into the new zero-free region creates two competing error contributions; choosing the truncation height T to balance them yields the characteristic 3/5 and 1/5 exponents.
accepted_units.context_note: The contour-shift details are omitted in the source, so this unit supports the optimization logic but not a self-contained proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence; exact error terms and the optimal T are displayed.

accepted_units.title: The error term encodes deep cancellation yet remains far from the RH scale
accepted_units.why_material: The closing discussion separates qualitative applications of sharper errors from mere numerical refinement, identifies the zeta-sum estimate as the Fourier-analytic content transported to primes, and states that wider cancellation ranges would widen zero-free regions without providing a route to the critical line.
accepted_units.context_note: The RH comparison is a limitation and research-direction statement, not evidence that the method approaches RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-to-moderate formula dependence; the conceptual distinctions are prose-dominant.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Polynomialize, duplicate, count, and recover cancellation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Small bilinear shifts turn the logarithmic phase into a bounded-degree polynomial; independent variable families can then be duplicated until sparse curve data is expressed through mean-value counts and rational-spacing sums, whose combined savings return a nontrivial original zeta-sum bound.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The synthesis is conditional on the source's scale and parameter regime; it does not claim square-root cancellation or applicability to arbitrary phases.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Translation-invariant scale descent handles both regular and degenerate residues
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Distinct residues give prime-power rigidity through symmetric polynomials, while too few residues reduce pattern entropy; common translation and division by the matched prime convert both branches into smaller-scale mean values.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This describes the architecture of the stated classical induction and does not substitute for its formula-sensitive exponent bookkeeping.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local cancellation propagates through analytic interfaces to prime distribution
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The short-sum estimate is transferred by partial/Abel summation to zeta growth, then by Landau's theorem to a zero-free strip, and finally by contour shifting and truncation optimization to a prime-number-theorem error term.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several interface theorems and contour details are referenced from earlier notes rather than proved here, so the chain is source-supported but not self-contained.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The useful diagnostic is the cancellation range, not only the final error's shape
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The theorem's mathematical content is exposed by how far below fixed powers of t it controls zeta sums; improving that range would widen zero-free regions, while the current range remains structurally remote from the critical-line prediction.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source offers no plausible route from this method to RH and explicitly frames the gap as unresolved.
